newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria share prices fall further with index.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria share prices fall further with index.

text.p: Nigerian share prices fell on Friday for the second successive day. The all-share index closed at 8685.04 from 8688.83 on Thursday.
Oil stocks were hard hit. African Petroleum fell 20 kobo, the same margin as Union Bank to 58.00 naira and 15.00 naira, respectively.

Unipetrol extended its string of recent losses by 10 kobo, the same loss it sustained on Thursday and now stands at 69.80 naira. Agip, which dropped by 90 kobo on Thursday shaved another three kobo on Friday to 22.97 naira.
"Pricing is now very cautious because there is nothing to drive the market up," said one broker.
Results by conglomerate UAC did not move the market. It was untraded at 18.40 naira.
Afribank, Nigeria's fourth largest bank, extended its 10 kobo loss of Thursday by a similar margin to 6.80 naira.
Gainers were few, led by oil company Texaco which rose by 20 kobo to 48.80 naira while the rarely-traded hospital stock Ekocorp rose 15 kobo to 4.25 naira.
Newly-listed Guaranty Trust Bank gained 10 kobo to 12.50 naira.
"The outlook is uncertain with nothing in the horizon to move the market," commented one dealer.
